power: Set the default keyboard wakeup capability to enabled. As part of crrev.com/c/1069220, we deleted the udev rule that tries to control the wakeup capability of internal keyboard. The reason for the change was powerd and EC seem to get into a race to control wakes from internal keyboard. Please look at crbug.com/836279 for more details. After this change powerd stopped worrying abount internal keyboard. This will be a problem if the default value of power/wakeup property of the internal keyboard is set to disabled for 2 reasons. 1. If the default state is disabled, and if the user presses a key when the kernel is in the suspend path, power core in the kernel will not abort the suspend. 2. Dark resume will not work as we cannot attribute wakeups to keybaord since the wakeup count will not increment if the property is set to disabled. To fix this on the ARM side, we set the default state to enabled(crrev.com/c/1101959). On the intel side we use atkbd driver, which is a generic driver. I highly doubt a patch to set the default state will be accepted. Thus instead set the default value to enabled in powerd. How was this not a problem on recent devices? It so happened that most of the devices that we build recently have side buttons. Thus we install a option udev rule 93-powerd-tags-keyboard-side-buttons.rules which enables wakeup. How was this not a problem on nocturne? Though nocturne does not have side buttons, nocturne does not use atkbd driver for internal keyboard. Since the internal keyboard is on usb bus, wake is enabled by default. Will this change cause any regressions on older devices? It should not. First on intel devices, only kernel honours this property. ACPI does not. Thus if keyboard causes any spurious wakes, previously device would end up in a suspend resume loop as kernel suspends and ec would wake the system immediately. Now the suspend fails. Thus the system would try for 10 times and shuts down instead. Thus this should only improve the situation. On ARM devices this property is set to enabled by default anyway. BUG=b:133262012 TEST=Run power_WakeSources and make sure the INTERNAL_KEYBOARD passes. common: Add EC_CMD_LOCATE_CHIP This patch replaces EC_CMD_I2C_LOOKUP with EC_CMD_LOCATE_CHIP. This is a more generic command which locates a peripheral chip in i2c or other bus types. Additionally, it includes the following changes: - Change chip (device) type # of CBI_EEPROM (from 1 to 0). - Support TCPCs. localhost ~ # ectool locatechip 0 0 BUS: I2C; Port: 0; Address: 0x50 (7-bit format) localhost ~ # ectool locatechip 1 0 BUS: I2C; Port: 0; Address: 0x0b (7-bit format) localhost ~ # ectool locatechip 1 1 BUS: I2C; Port: 1; Address: 0x29 (7-bit format) localhost ~ # ectool locatechip 1 2 EC result 11 (OVERFLOW) Index too large localhost ~ # ectool locatechip 2 Usage: locatechip <type> <index> <type> is one of: 0: CBI_EEPROM 1: TCPCs <index> instance # of <type> Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=Verified ectool locatechip work on Nami. Change-Id: I1a773ced65b1c5ce3656f03eff04a6eadd4bc5ff Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1614582 Commit-Ready: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: sysctl: Add sysctl to lock core_pattern |core_pattern| gets routinely abused to achieve persistent exploitation. Lock down core pattern once the system has booted up and disallow modifications once the lock is set. This means that the |core_pattern| set here is now finalized for this boot. This will only be used for kernels trees before 4.4: usermode-helper helps effectively filter out coredump requests in newer kernels. UPSTREAM: efi/x86/Add missing error handling to old_memmap 1:1 mapping code The old_memmap flow in efi_call_phys_prolog() performs numerous memory allocations, and either does not check for failure at all, or it does but fails to propagate it back to the caller, which may end up calling into the firmware with an incomplete 1:1 mapping. So let's fix this by returning NULL from efi_call_phys_prolog() on memory allocation failures only, and by handling this condition in the caller. Also, clean up any half baked sets of page tables that we may have created before returning with a NULL return value. Note that any failure at this level will trigger a panic() two levels up, so none of this makes a huge difference, but it is a nice cleanup nonetheless. [ardb: update commit log, add efi_call_phys_epilog() call on error path] BUG=chromium:968987 TEST=None Change-Id: Ide8d514a3c02d03385ec0e9bd7fd2b813a021f12 Signed-off-by: Gen Zhang <blackgod016574@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Ard Biesheuvel <ard.biesheuvel@linaro.org> Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org> Cc: Rob Bradford <robert.bradford@intel.com> Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de> Cc: linux-efi@vger.kernel.org Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190525112559.7917-2-ard.biesheuvel@linaro.org Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 4e78921ba4dd0aca1cc89168f45039add4183f8e) Signed-off-by: Zubin Mithra <zsm@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1639755 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Zubin Mithra <zsm@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Zubin Mithra <zsm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>
